question: Which Swiss residential sites contain equivalent or tightly matched room-area arrangements and should be kept together before deriving scenes or assigning splits?
selection: All RESIDENTIAL unit area polygons on the numerically smallest floor_id of each source site/building/plan. Every site remains unallocated. No rendering, native room creation, source simulation values or inferred professional labels.
limitations: Only area polygon arrangements, not doors/windows/fixtures or vertical dimensions.
Geometric similarity proposes conservative leakage grouping; not physical-project identity or proof of statistical independence.
Nominal source plan IDs choose one floor; within-plan geometry variation on unselected floors not audited.
Near retrieval requires equal area-polygon count and four size descriptors within five percent; different subdivisions and larger edits can be missed.
Rotated bounding rectangle alignment can be unstable under some perturbations; no exhaustive near-duplicate recall guarantee.
Invalid/degenerate/single-area units are excluded from shape matching and remain unresolved.
Mirror and rotation matches concern split leakage; original north/daylight orientation must remain intact for later scene inputs.
Transitive geometry groups may overgroup unrelated projects; do not treat their size as number of original design families.
No automatic train/dev/test allocation; source example site127 stays development-restricted.
change: Center unit polygons before calling GEOS minimum_rotated_rectangle; require covering rectangle and finite positive edges. Same corpus, representative floors, candidate gates and budgets; no source geometry edited. New source regression included.
